s: mountains is a mountain range (with steep sides)
q: Jinxland is separated from the rest of the Quadling Country by that row of high mountains you see yonder, which have such steep sides that no one can cross them.

s: mountains is uncrossable by people (because of its steep sides)

q: "It belongs to his Majesty, King Krewl." she said.

s: King Krewl rules Jinxland (as its own king)
q: So we live here all by ourselves, and are ruled by our own King, instead of by Ozma of Oz."

s: King Krewl punishes treason (severely)
q: "The King punishes severely any treason on the part of his subjects."

s: King Krewl is associated with the fierce courtiers and war captains (when hunting)
q: "When he is not out hunting with his fierce courtiers and war captains," she replied.

s: the King's castle belongs to King Krewl

q: They believed this path would lead them to a splendid castle which they espied in the distance, the turrets of which towered far above the tops of the trees which surrounded it.

q: The woman sent the children into the house. Then she came closer to the strangers and whispered: "If only we had a different King, we would be very happy and contented."

s: the children of the cottage are curious about Cap'n Bill (because of his wooden leg)

l: Tik-Tok of Oz, Tik-Tok of Oz, Chapter One
s: Ann Soforth, Queen of Oogaboo, becomes dissatisfied with her small kingdom and decides to conquer the world, beginning with the Land of Oz. Salye's taunt inspires Ann to raise an army of Oogaboo's eighteen men, most of whom she assigns high military ranks. Jo Candy refuses to join, while Jo Files agrees to serve as the sole Private and promises to find a gun-tree. Ann's Army is assembled with four Generals, four Colonels, four Majors, four Captains, two prospective Lieutenants, and Jo Files as Private, though only sixteen men have joined.

l: Queen Ann, Tik-Tok of Oz, Chapter One
s: Ann Soforth is the eldest daughter of Oogaboo's royal family and acts as Queen after her mother leaves in search of King Jol Jemkiph Soforth. Dissatisfied with ruling a tiny, poor kingdom, she decides to conquer the world and organizes an army of Oogaboo's men.

l: Salye, Tik-Tok of Oz, Chapter One
s: Salye, Ann Soforth's younger sister, refuses to sweep the palace floor and taunts Ann by suggesting that she raise an army and conquer the Land of Oz. She then goes into the back yard to swing in a hammock.

l: Queen Ann of Oogaboo, Tik-Tok of Oz, Chapter One
s: The Queen of Oogaboo is Ann Soforth, who rules eighteen men, twenty-seven women, and forty-four children. She decides that conquering the peaceful Land of Oz will allow her to replace Princess Ozma as ruler.

l: Ozma of Oz, Tik-Tok of Oz, Chapter One
s: Princess Ozma rules the Land of Oz from the Emerald City and is loved and obeyed by her people. Her army is said to consist of twenty-seven unarmed officers, and she once made her only private soldier a Captain-General and took away his gun.

l: Oogaboo, Tik-Tok of Oz, Chapter One
s: Oogaboo is a small, poor valley in a remote mountainous corner of the Land of Oz. It has a royal family for pride, while its people remain under Princess Ozma's overall rule.

l: Land of Oz, Tik-Tok of Oz, Chapter One
s: The Land of Oz is a beautiful fairyland ruled by Princess Ozma from the Emerald City. Ann considers it peaceful and believes its unarmed officers and gentle people will be easy to overcome.

l: world, Tik-Tok of Oz, Chapter One
s: Ann declares that she intends to conquer the world, beginning with the Land of Oz. She later imagines conquering other lands and possibly even the moon.

l: Army of Oogaboo, Tik-Tok of Oz, Chapter One
s: Ann's Army is formed from the men of Oogaboo for her planned conquest. Four men become Generals, four Colonels, four Majors, and four Captains; Jo Files becomes the sole Private, while Jo Candy refuses to join.

l: Files, Tik-Tok of Oz, Chapter One
s: Jo Files is a young, intelligent, ambitious man whose orchards produce steel files and story-books. He refuses the officer ranks and volunteers to be the sole Private in Ann's Army, claiming that he will do the fighting; he also knows where to find a gun-tree and plans to pick a musket.

l: the Oogaboo expedition to conquer the world, Tik-Tok of Oz, Chapter One
s: Ann plans the conquest of Oz because she believes Princess Ozma's peaceful, unarmed forces can be defeated through surprise and intimidation. She expects to set herself up as ruler in Ozma's place without shedding blood.

l: Ann's venture, Tik-Tok of Oz, Chapter One
s: Ann's venture begins when she leaves the palace to organize an army for her proposed conquest. She believes the venture cannot make her less happy than remaining in Oogaboo and accepts the risks in hopes of gaining greater power.

l: Tik-Tok of Oz, Tik-Tok of Oz, Chapter Two
s: Three days after Queen Ann Soforth's decision to conquer the world, the Grand Army of Oogaboo assembles outside the royal palace. Ann orders the protesting women to be silent and leads her sixteen officers and the Private, Files, in the army's departure. The officers and Files pass orders down the ranks until Files begins marching, followed by the officers and then Queen Ann. The procession leaves Oogaboo through a narrow mountain pass toward Fairyland of Oz, seeking plunder and fame.

l: Oogaboo, Tik-Tok of Oz, Chapter Two
s: Oogaboo's Grand Army assembles in the square before the royal palace. The army then marches out of Oogaboo through a narrow mountain pass toward Fairyland of Oz.

l: Army of Oogaboo, Tik-Tok of Oz, Chapter Two
s: The Grand Army of Oogaboo consists of sixteen officers and the Private, Files. Its members wear impressive uniforms and carry weapons, but General Bunn says they seek plunder rather than trouble and prefer to avoid fighting.

l: Queen Ann, Tik-Tok of Oz, Chapter Two
s: Queen Ann Soforth appears in a green and gold uniform, commands the protesting women to keep silent, and orders her Army to form ranks. She leads the army out of Oogaboo, expecting it to return rich and famous through conquest, plunder, and heroism.

l: Files, Tik-Tok of Oz, Chapter Two
s: Files is the Private in the army and carries a gun, which he has picked. He looks fierce enough to make his commanding officers secretly afraid of him, and he begins the march after receiving the order passed down through the ranks.

l: plunder, Tik-Tok of Oz, Chapter Two
s: Plunder is the main objective of Queen Ann Soforth's campaign. General Bunn says the army wants as much plunder and as little fighting as possible, while Ann connects securing plunder with conquest and becoming heroes.

l: Land of Oz, Tik-Tok of Oz, Chapter Two
s: Fairyland of Oz lies beyond the narrow mountain pass leading out of Oogaboo. The army takes this pass as it begins its campaign.

l: army departure and march, Tik-Tok of Oz, Chapter Two
s: The army departs after the Generals, Colonels, Majors, and Captains pass the command "For-ward March!" down the ranks to Files. Files marches first, the officers follow, and Queen Ann comes last as the procession enters the mountain pass toward Fairyland of Oz.

l: Tik-Tok of Oz, Tik-Tok of Oz, Chapter Three
s: Princess Ozma is unaware that Ann Soforth and the Army of Oogaboo intend to invade and conquer the Land of Oz. Glinda the Good learns of the plan through her Magic Record Book and uses magic to redirect the mountain pass, sending the army into an adjoining territory instead of Oz. Lost and hungry, the army encounters a Rak, which Private Files wounds with his gun before leading Queen Ann away from it. The army later reaches a valley, camps beside a brook, and continues to claim that it has begun the conquest of the world.

l: Ozma of Oz, Tik-Tok of Oz, Chapter Three
s: Princess Ozma is busy caring for her subjects and is unaware of Ann Soforth's plan to invade the Land of Oz.

l: Land of Oz, Tik-Tok of Oz, Chapter Three
s: The Land of Oz is protected from the Army of Oogaboo's intended invasion when Glinda redirects the mountain pass into another territory.

l: Glinda the Good, Tik-Tok of Oz, Chapter Three
s: Glinda the Good, the Official Sorceress of the Kingdom, guards the peace of the Land of Oz. After learning of the army's plan, she uses magic to alter the mountain pass so the army does not enter Oz.

l: Queen Ann, Tik-Tok of Oz, Chapter Three
s: Ann Soforth, Queen of Oogaboo, leads her army toward the Land of Oz intending to conquer it and the world. When the army reaches an unknown territory instead, she decides to conquer whatever land they find and later praises Private Files for his courage.

l: Army of Oogaboo, Tik-Tok of Oz, Chapter Three
s: The Army of Oogaboo consists of sixteen officers and one private soldier under Ann Soforth. It becomes lost in an unknown, barren country, grows hungry and discouraged, encounters a Rak, and eventually camps beside a brook.

l: Oogaboo, Tik-Tok of Oz, Chapter Three
s: Oogaboo is the army's homeland, a pretty valley with orchards. After the army passes through the altered mountain route, its members cannot find their way back there.

l: magic Record Book of the Sorceress Glinda, Tik-Tok of Oz, Chapter Three
s: Glinda's Magic Record Book records every event that takes place anywhere, from small incidents to great disasters. By reading it, Glinda learns that Ann Soforth has assembled an army to invade the Land of Oz.

l: mountain pass from Oogaboo, Tik-Tok of Oz, Chapter Three
s: Glinda performs a magical ceremony that causes the mountain pass from Oogaboo to make several turns and twists. After the army emerges into the adjoining territory, the pass disappears behind it.

l: adjoining territory, Tik-Tok of Oz, Chapter Three
s: The adjoining territory is distinct from the Land of Oz and separated from it by an invisible barrier. The Army of Oogaboo enters it without realizing at first that it has failed to reach Oz.

l: the officers of Oogaboo, Tik-Tok of Oz, Chapter Three
s: The sixteen officers travel with Ann Soforth through the strange country and become hungry, fretful, and disloyal. When the Rak appears, they panic, fall to the ground, and later run away when it rolls off them.

l: Files, Tik-Tok of Oz, Chapter Three
s: Private Files remains cheerful during the army's hardships and becomes a trusted adviser to Queen Ann. He recognizes the approaching cloud as possibly the breath of a Rak, shoots the creature with his gun, and leads the Queen away after the officers flee.

l: Rak, Tik-Tok of Oz, Chapter Three
s: The Rak is described as a huge flying, running, and swimming beast that breathes smoke, has a furnace-like body, and feeds on living things. Private Files's bullets break its jaw, left wing, and right leg, but it says that its injuries will heal and that it bears a charmed life.

l: the Oogaboo expedition to conquer the world, Tik-Tok of Oz, Chapter Three
s: Ann Soforth says that the army has started out to conquer the world and treats the unknown territory as part of that objective. Private Files refuses to remain with the Rak because he has an engagement to help Queen Ann achieve the conquest.

l: invasion and conquest of the Land of Oz, Tik-Tok of Oz, Chapter Three
s: Ann Soforth assembles the Army of Oogaboo for an invasion and conquest of the Land of Oz. Glinda prevents the army from reaching Oz by changing the route through the mountain pass.

l: the Army's journey, Tik-Tok of Oz, Chapter Three
s: The army's journey takes it through a barren, rocky country where it finds little food and becomes hopelessly lost. On the third day it encounters the Rak, then travels beyond the creature's smoky breath and camps by a brook.

l: the Rak's attack, Tik-Tok of Oz, Chapter Three
s: The Rak's smoky breath darkens the sky and envelops the army, while its body falls upon the sixteen officers after Files shoots it. The Rak tries to crush and eat the army, but it rolls away from the officers, allowing them to escape.

l: magic, Tik-Tok of Oz, Chapter Three
s: Glinda uses magic to alter the mountain pass and divert the Army of Oogaboo from the Land of Oz. The army also possesses magical travel equipment, including tents and a table that grow when placed on the ground.

l: gun (Files's gun), Tik-Tok of Oz, Chapter Three
s: Files's gun is loaded with large, hard bullets gathered from a bullet-tree in Oogaboo. He fires it at the Rak, breaking the creature's jaw, left wing, and right leg.

l: Tik-Tok of Oz, Tik-Tok of Oz, Chapter Four
s: Betsy Bobbin and Hank, a thin, sad-faced mule, are thrown into the sea when their ship strikes a rock during a storm. Betsy grabs Hank's tail, then helps him climb onto a floating hatch-cover that becomes their raft after the ship catches fire, explodes, and sinks. They endure the night on the raft, and Hank stays awake to guard Betsy while she sleeps. At dawn, they see a beautiful, apparently uninhabited land ahead.

l: Betsy Bobbin, Tik-Tok of Oz, Chapter Four
s: Betsy is thrown from the ship into the sea when it strikes a rock. She grabs Hank's tail, helps him aboard a floating hatch-cover, and rides with him through the storm. After sleeping on the raft, she wakes at dawn and sees land ahead.

l: Hank, Tik-Tok of Oz, Chapter Four
s: Hank, a thin, sad-faced mule, is thrown into the sea with Betsy. He swims to the raft, and Betsy helps him climb aboard. He comforts Betsy, promises to protect her, and stays awake through the night while she sleeps.

l: ship, Tik-Tok of Oz, Chapter Four
s: The ship strikes a rock during the storm. After Betsy and Hank are thrown overboard, it catches fire, blows up, and sinks beneath the waves.

l: storm, Tik-Tok of Oz, Chapter Four
s: The storm brings waves, lightning, and thunder while the ship is wrecked. It continues after the ship sinks, then wears itself out and passes away with distant growls.

l: sea, Tik-Tok of Oz, Chapter Four
s: Betsy and Hank fall into the dark blue sea after the ship strikes a rock. They float on the raft through the night, while the waves gradually become smaller and easier to ride.

l: raft (Betsy's and Hank's raft), Tik-Tok of Oz, Chapter Four
s: The raft is a hatch-cover torn from the ship's deck. Betsy pulls herself onto it, and Hank swims to it and climbs aboard with her help. It keeps them from drowning and carries them toward land.

l: shipwreck, Tik-Tok of Oz, Chapter Four
s: The shipwreck occurs when the ship strikes a rock during the storm. The ship catches fire, explodes, and sinks, leaving Betsy and Hank on a floating hatch-cover.

l: adjoining territory, Tik-Tok of Oz, Chapter Four
s: At dawn, Betsy sees land ahead. It appears to be a very beautiful country with banks of flowers between leafy trees, but no people are visible.

l: Tik-Tok of Oz, Tik-Tok of Oz, Chapter Five
s: Betsy and Hank reach shore on a raft and discover a greenhouse in the Rose Kingdom. Inside, they find rosebushes bearing Roses with girls’ faces, who are frightened by Hank’s braying and demand that the refugees leave. The Roses explain that only Roses are allowed in the kingdom and that the Royal Gardener may cast strangers back into the sea. When the Royal Gardener arrives, he panics at Hank, invokes the Law of the Rose Kingdom, and is interrupted when a man crashes through the greenhouse roof.

l: Betsy Bobbin, Tik-Tok of Oz, Chapter Five
s: Betsy wades ashore from the raft with Hank and enters the greenhouse seeking people, food, and shelter. She explains that she and Hank survived a shipwreck by floating ashore on a raft, and she defends Hank when the Roses and the Royal Gardener are frightened by him.

l: Hank, Tik-Tok of Oz, Chapter Five
s: Hank follows Betsy ashore and into the greenhouse. His loud braying startles the Roses and causes the Royal Gardener to throw a watering pot over his head; Hank becomes angry and backs toward the Gardener threateningly.

l: raft (Betsy's and Hank's raft), Tik-Tok of Oz, Chapter Five
s: The raft carrying Betsy and Hank gently reaches the sandy beach. Betsy and Hank had caught hold of it after their ship was wrecked and floated ashore.

l: greenhouse, Tik-Tok of Oz, Chapter Five
s: The greenhouse is a large, splendid structure with thousands of crystal panes. It is filled with potted rosebushes bearing magnificent Roses with girls’ faces, and a man later falls through its roof.
